sources.title: A path integral method for solution of the wave equation with continuously-varying coefficients
sources.author_evidence: Not independently established in the returned metadata/passages used here.
sources.supported_claim: For its spatially varying acoustic medium, path-volume bounds give factorial series convergence and finite truncation estimates including derivative-series control. Faster alternating bounds have additional monotone-impedance/contrast/data hypotheses.
sources.use: Motivates estimating the actual causal integration geometry and preserving signed cancellation before taking absolute values.
sources.transfer_limit: A spatially varying acoustic impedance problem is not the HDB time-dependent-potential plus dynamic-boundary problem. Its factorial and alternating-tail constants require a separate operator proof before application.

sources.supported_claim: The paper proves strong boundary/bulk energy estimates for specified wave boundary conditions and describes a local quasilinear extension to the harmonic Einstein system.
sources.use: Methodological evidence that the nonlinear boundary structure and a constraint-preserving hierarchy must enter a well-posedness argument.
sources.transfer_limit: Sommerfeld-type boundary conditions differ from an Israel shell with scalar matter. No quantitative second-parameter-derivative bound, effective epsilon radius or nonlinear remainder is supplied for HDB by the retrieved passages.

sources.title: The initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equations with totally geodesic timelike boundary
sources.author_evidence: Not independently established in the returned metadata/passages used here.
locators: Abstract statement of anisotropic normal-derivative difficulty
sources.supported_claim: The Einstein vacuum boundary problem uses a totally geodesic timelike boundary, anisotropic boundary regularity and cancellation of boundary energy fluxes in the propagation of constraints. The returned proposition uses B^s with s>=7 for its boundary argument.
sources.use: Shows that even an Einstein vacuum boundary proof relies on boundary-specific flux and normal-derivative structure.
sources.transfer_limit: The totally geodesic vacuum boundary is not an Einstein-scalar Israel shell. The B^s scale is not ordinary H^s. No HDB shell remainder or numerical parameter range follows.

sources.title: Optimal error bounds on the exponential integrator for dispersive equations with highly concentrated potential
sources.supported_claim: The returned abstract describes cancellation-sensitive iterated-Duhamel analysis and an exponential integrator for a one-dimensional dispersive equation with concentrated potential.
sources.transfer_limit: Body, authors and applicability were not independently verified. The dispersive equation and integration method do not directly cover the present hyperbolic endpoint-mass problem.
